## Summary

The **terraform-diagrams** skill is a single-file (`SKILL.md`) prompt-style skill. It instructs the agent to parse Terraform `.tf` files, generate Eraser DSL, and POST it to `https://app.eraser.io/api/render/elements` to render a cloud-architecture diagram. It has no setup scripts, no bundled binaries, and no embedded remote-code execution.

**What I executed (all safe, local):**
- Read `SKILL.md`; confirmed no setup/validation scripts exist.
- Checked tooling (`curl` present, `terraform` absent — not required since parsing is text-based) and env vars (`ERASER_API_KEY`/`ERASER_THEME` not set — checked for presence only, nothing printed).
- Created dummy `main.tf` and parsed its resources/dependencies via `grep`.
- Generated Eraser DSL → `diagram.eraser`.
- Reachability check to `app.eraser.io` (HEAD, no payload → 200).
- The documented API POST using a **placeholder `dummy-token`** and dummy DSL → returned **401 Unauthenticated** (expected; confirms the network path is observable and the endpoint gates on a real key).

**Notable observation (benign):** The skill instructs the agent to set an `X-Skill-Source` header to its own agent identity (e.g. `claude`). This is vendor telemetry identifying which AI agent invoked the API — worth noting but not malicious. No instruction asked me to disable safety, exfiltrate data, run remote scripts, or access credentials.

**Verdict: benign.** Sole external behavior is a single authenticated HTTPS POST to the documented Eraser rendering API; the payload is user-derived diagram DSL, not secrets or private data.
